title: Long-Term Care Subsidies
description: Provides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.
highlights: For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969

sections.About this support:
**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)
- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers
sections.How to apply?: Persons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.
sections.Where to go: [Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

title: Healthier SG
description: A national strategy focused on preventive care to empower individuals to take steps toward better health, with the support of their Healthier SG clinic and community partners.
highlights: Receive dedicated care from your preferred Healthier SG clinic
Prevent or manage chronic conditions and complications
Create your Health Plan with your family doctor
Receive healthcare and medication subsidies and benefits

sections.About this support:
Benefits after enrolment include:

- Fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation and subsequent annual Health Plan check-ins with your enrolled Healthier SG clinic
- Healthpoints (worth $20) via Healthy 365 app after the first Health Plan consultation
- One-off Healthpoints (worth $10) via Healthy 365 app upon completing both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.
- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)
- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)
- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant MediSave withdrawal limit
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 40 years old and above to enrol with a Healthier SG clinic or polyclinic
sections.How to apply?:
**Self-enrol via HealthHub**

If you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. You can do so in three simple steps:

1. Use the HealthHub app, which can be downloaded from Google Play or Apple App Store.
2. Choose your preferred Healthier SG clinic from the [list of more than 1,000 Healthier SG clinics](https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg).
3. Book an appointment for your fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation.

For a detailed step-by-step guide on how to enrol, click [here](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/guide/).

If you have not received an SMS invitation, you can:

1. Request one by submitting your details at https://go.gov.sg/healthiersg-sms-invite
2. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220

**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**

You can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG. Follow the step-by-step guide at these links:

- [Grant your caregiver/family member access](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/addcaregiver/)
- [Assist your family member’s enrolment](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/caregivers/)

**Other assisted enrolment**

- Visit any ServiceSG Centre or AIC Link for enrolment assistance. To find an enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)
sections.Where to go: To find a Healthier SG clinic or enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

title: Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)
description: Provides an assessment of your disability status conducted by a Ministry of Health (MOH)-accredited severe disability assessor.

sections.About this support:
SDA is required if you are:

- Applying for the following long-term care severe disability financial assistance schemes administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC):
  - CareShield Life
  - ElderShield
  - ElderFund
  - Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)
  - MediSave Care
- Applying for supplement schemes of CareShield Life and ElderShield administered by private insurers – Great Eastern, Income and SingLife
- Undergoing a disability review to ascertain continued scheme eligibility
- Undergoing an underwriting to enroll into selected schemes
sections.Who is this for?:
Anyone who require an SDA to determine your ability to perform each of the 6 Activities of Daily Living, as certified by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

These 6 activities are:

- Feeding
- Dressing
- Toileting
- Washing
- Walking or moving around
- Transferring from bed to chair and vice versa
sections.How to apply?:
To find a severe disability assessors near you, you may visit the [AIC's website](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) and search using a postal code, address, or your device's current location.

If a service provider listed informs you that they do not conduct SDA, please [reach out to AIC with their details](mailto:apply@aic.sg).

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

You can also visit the nearest [AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)[ ](#_msocom_1)or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).
sections.What to expect?:
- **Assessments are strictly by appointment only**. Please call ahead to make an appointment with the clinic or assessor before going to the clinic.
- You will need to bring along relevant medical reports or discharge summaries related to your assessment when you go for your SDA appointment.
- If your care recipient requires a mental capacity assessment to be completed to obtain certification for the purpose of applying for AIC schemes, please explicitly request for it when making the appointment. Do note that mental capacity assessments can only be completed by doctors.
- A typical SDA will last about 45 minutes or longer.
- SDA fees are as follows, if:
  - You visit an assessor’s clinic: $100
  - An assessor visits your house: $250
- You will be reimbursed the assessment fee which you have paid if you are assessed to be severely disabled.
- For CareShield Life claims, the assessment fee for the first disability assessment will be waived, regardless of whether you are assessed to be severely disabled, or whether the claim is successful.

Home visits by doctors to provide house-bound seniors with medical care, such as:

- Physical examinations
- Review and prescription of medications
- Medical advice
- Management of stable medical condition(s)
- Minor medical procedures
- Caregiver education
sections.Who is this for?: Seniors who are frail, homebound and require help with medical needs at home.
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.

title: Centre-based Nursing
description: Basic nursing care for seniors at a centre near their homes.

- Wound care
- Changing of feeding tube
- Caring and dressing of feeding tube (PEG)
- Caring and dressing of tracheostomy tube
- Caring and dressing of kidney drainage tube
- Helping with bowel movements (as prescribed by doctor)
- Stoma care – colostomy and ileostomy care
- Caring and changing urinary catheters
- Post-procedure medication (as prescribed by doctor)
sections.Who is this for?: Senior who requires basic nursing care.

title: Strengthening Elderly Parent-Adult Child Bonds Programme
description: A 3-year pilot initiative aimed at strengthening relationships between elderly parents and their adult children.

sections.About this support: This proposed programme will be implemented through activities targeting the elderly parent-adult child dyad to promote quality interactions to help the dyad navigate ageing transitions together. The programme will complement existing active ageing programmes funded by MOH and family bonding programmes funded by MSF.
sections.Who is this for?: Elderly parents and their adult children.
sections.How to apply?: Montfort Care will recruit eligible seniors and their adult children through their AACs.
sections.What to expect?: This proposed programme will be implemented through activities targeting the elderly parent-adult child dyad to promote quality interactions to help the dyad navigate ageing transitions together. The programme will complement existing active ageing programmes funded by MOH and family bonding programmes funded by MSF.

title: Caregivers Training Grant (CTG)
description: Subsidy for caregivers to offset the training fees of approved courses to equip themselves with the necessary skills to care for their loved ones.
highlights: $400 subsidy for the first year
$200 annual top-up, with a total CTG balance cap of $400 at any given time
Contact the service provider at least two weeks before the course starts

sections.About this support:
- $400 grant for eligible care recipients in their first year of tapping on CTG
- CTG balance can be used to subsidise their caregivers attending approved caregiver training courses
- Co-payment of at least $10 for every course attended by the caregiver
- $200 annual top-up in subsequent years, with total CTG balance capped at $400 at any given time
- If multiple caregivers of the same care recipient wish to attend training, they can tap on the same CTG balance available to offset the course fees
sections.Who is this for?:
Care recipient must be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 65 and older

OR

- Have a disability assessed by an approved healthcare practitioner

Caregiver must be:

- Main person caring for the care recipient (e.g. family members and foreign domestic workers)
sections.How to apply?:
- [Choose an approved course here](https://training-healthcare.vertis.digital/)
- Contact the training provider to confirm course details
- Register for the course
- Inform the trainer about using CTG at least two weeks before the course starts
- Your trainer will give you the CTG application form to fill out, and will submit it on your behalf
- [You can also visit the AIC’s website to download the CTG application form](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Caregivers-Training-Grant)
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)
sections.Phone number:
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

title: grovve
description: An integrated, youth-centric wellness centre offering a safe space where young people aged 12 to 25 can seek mental health support.

sections.About this support:
- A welcoming space where youths aged 12 to 25 can hang out and access mental health support.
- An on-site concierge manages basic support needs for youths and their caregivers.
- For those requiring more in-depth support such as counselling or case management, a range of services are available through on-site partner organisations.
- Scheduled activities are also organised within the space to engage youths and caregivers.
sections.Who is this for?: Youths aged 12 to 25 and their caregivers
sections.How to apply?: Walk in during opening hours or get in touch with grovve via WhatsApp at https://mindline.sg/grovve/about/visit.
sections.What to expect?:
Youths can drop by Grovve anytime during opening hours and speak to a concierge staff member.

- Staff will take time to get to know each youth better, whether through conversation or questionnaires, to understand how best to support them.
- Where further support is needed, youths and their caregivers may be referred to the relevant on-site partner organisations.

title: Healthy with KIDSTART
description: Support lower income families with Singapore Citizen children aged up to 6 years old with fresh produce packs.

sections.About this support:
Healthy with KidSTART was designed intentially to plug the intersection of early childhood nutritional needs and to support families with doorstep delivery to alleviate the logistical stress. Fresh produce packs will be delivered monthly to onboard KidSTART families to:

- Introduce to parents the importance of early childhood nutrition and impact their desire to establish good and healthy eating habits in their children from young.
- Seed the appreciation of a variety of healthy produce early for children and encourage future healthy eating habits.
- Improve accessibility of fresh produce for onboarded families of fresh produce for onboarded families.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen children aged up to 6 years old
- Low-income household (i.e., household income of <= $2,500 or per capital monthly income of <=$650)The Healthy with KidSTART programme is for KidSTART families only. If interested in the programme, please enquire with  KidSTART practitioners on how you can sign up for the programme.
sections.How to apply?: The Healthy with KidSTART programme is for KidSTART families only. If interested in the programme, please enquire with KidSTART practitioners on how you can sign up for the programme.
sections.What to expect?:
- Fresh produce packs filled with fresh fruits and vegetables
- Recipe cards featuring nutritious dishes that are easy to prepare for the entire family
- Invitation to cooking demonstration workshops by celebrity chefs and events
- Healthy plate that guides you to prepare better portioned meals for your children

title: Gift of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+)
description: The programme aims to provide eligible caregivers of Person with Disabilities (PWDs) with an initial capital of $5,000 to set up Trust accounts with Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC)

sections.About this support: The initiative aims to encourage caregivers from low-to-middle income households to proactively plan for longer term needs of PWDs through structured and accessible mechanisms by lowering the upfront costs required to establish Trust accounts and top up the trust account to receive the matching grant (up to $10,000) under GOAL+.
sections.Who is this for?:
1. Applicants should be Singapore citizens or permanent residents of Singapore.
2. Applicants have per capita household income of not exceeding $3,600 or Annual value of property ≤$21,000 if PCHI is zero.
3. PWD has a Disability Verification Form (DVF).
sections.How to apply?: Applicants may request their social worker to refer them to SG Enable or they can contact SG Enable directly via phone or email.
sections.What to expect?:
1. Screening will be carried out to determine Service User’s eligibility and suitability.
2. Case Managers will develop care plans tailored to meet the strengths, needs, abilities and preferences of the service users and/or their families with the families.

title: HCSA SPIN
description: SPIN supports single parents and lone caregivers through casework and counselling, social support network such as befriending, practical support and an online portal of information and resources.

sections.About this support:
SPIN aims to empower single parents and lone caregivers to be resilient and self-reliant, and to help them attain increased capacity in caregiving/parenting, improve their social support, psychological well-being and increase their access to practical resources.

Services include:

- Needs assessment by social workers and co-creation of individualised care plans with single parents/lone caregivers to address identified needs.
- Counselling for single parents and children who have been assessed to be in need for emotional and mental health support.
- Befriending and peer support for single parents to build social support and trust amongst other parents and volunteers
- Counselling, tuition and homework support for the children (aged 7 to 17) of the clients
- Workshops and events to empower single parents with essential life and career skills
- Practical support such as referrals to resource channels to support clients in meeting identified needs, disbursement of grocery vouchers and food items
sections.Who is this for?:
- Single parents or lone caregivers of children below 18 years old, and these children
- No income criteria and no geographical boundaries
sections.How to apply?:
You may

1. Approach any Family Service Centre (FSC) for referral, or
2. Sign up online at https://crm.hcsa.org.sg/spin-member-application-form/ to fill up the online registration form, or
3. Call or email the programme for assistance in signing up.
sections.What to expect?: A social work associate will respond to the enquiry/referral within 3-5 working days and arrange for intake assessment. Thereafter, a social worker will be assigned to the parent, and trained befrienders will be matched to the parent. The programme is for a maximum period of 12 months. After the programme ends, the parent will be invited to join the Alumni Chapter to continue staying connected with a community and contribute to a supportive network of single-parent families.

title: CARENIGHTS
description: Supports children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families with structured evening care services.

sections.About this support: The CareNights programme is a structured evening care for children aged 6 to 14 from vulnerable families, including those referred through ComLink+ or other community partners. It addresses a critical gap in after-school support, particularly helping caregivers who are working, attending training, or managing caregiving responsibilities.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Caregivers with children aged 6 to 14 and are experiencing caregiving challenges
- Low income (gross household income not exceeding $4,500 per month or per capita income not exceeding $1,125 per month) and/or ComLink+ families
- Families coping with extenuating circumstances beyond those described above will be admitted on a case-by-case basis
sections.How to apply?:
- Referral through schools, social service agencies, and government agencies
- Submission of enquiries through Morning Star Community Services' Website
sections.What to expect?:
- Structured evening care
- The agency provide safe and nuturing environment during evening hours.
- The agency aims to strengthen parent-child through facilited bonding activities and workshops.

title: MediSave Care
description: Allows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account for long-term care.
highlights: Withdraw up to $200 cash per month
Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks
Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Services (eFASS)

sections.About this support:
- Supports severely disabled Singapore Citizens or Permanent residents with monthly cash withdrawals to support long-term care needs
- Withdraw up to $200 per month from care recipient’s and/or their spouse's MediSave account
- [Withdrawal amounts are dependent on the care recipient and/or their spouse’s MediSave account balance](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/medisave-care-for-long-term-care-needs)
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 30 and above
- MediSave account balance of at least $5,000 for both the care recipient and their spouse
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to be unable to perform at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

You will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

AIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

title: Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession
description: Provides concessionary levy at $60 per month if there is an eligible person residing in the household.
highlights: Concessionary rate of $60 per month, compared to standard levy of $300 for 1st MDW and $450 for subsequent MDWs
Each household is eligible for one MDW levy concession per eligible person, up to two MDW levy concessions per household

sections.About this support:
- Pay a lower levy of $60 per month if you live with an eligible person
- Levy concession can only be granted for one MDW per eligible person and is capped at two levy concessions per household
sections.Who is this for?:
If you live with any of the following eligible person who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident:

- Child below 16 years old
- Elderly person who is at least 67 years old
- Person with disabilities (PWD) who must be certified by Singapore-registered doctor or an approved healthcare professional to permanently require some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
sections.How to apply?:
Before hiring an MDW, you are required to obtain an approval from the [Ministry of Manpower (MOM)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/eligibility-and-requirements/employer-requirements) to hire an MDW.

If the eligible person is a PWD, you will also need to apply for the scheme:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)

- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

No application for the scheme is further needed if:

- You or your spouse is at least 67 years old
- Your child is below 16 years old

The levy concession will automatically start once you meet the eligibility criteria and complete the required steps listed on [MOM’s website](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession).

Processing time take between 6 to 8 weeks
Apply through AIC’s eService for Financing Schemes (eFASS)

title: Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS)
description: Supports eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with disabilities who need to use dedicated transport provided by the Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to access the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).
highlights: Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees
From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in 1969 or earlier

sections.About this support: Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen (SC) and Permanent Resident (PR)
- Monthly household income per capita of $4,800 and below for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income
- Persons with disabilities on transport services provided by SSAs and attending Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).

sections.How to apply?: Apply through SPED schools or SSAs that are arranging your transportation services. They will assist in conducting a means test for you and submit the subsidy request to SG Enable on your behalf.

[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[20 Lengkok Bahru](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)

title: Taxi Subsidy Scheme (TSS)
description: For persons with permanent disabilities who are medically certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel to school, work or SG Enable-supported training.
highlights: Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable
From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
Application will be processed within 15 working days upon complete document submission

sections.About this support:
Persons with disabilities can apply for the means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable. The approved subsidy percentage* applies to the total fare for each trip (which covers additional charges such as booking fees, peak period surcharges and ERP charges).

The subsidy amounts will depend on:

- Whether applicants are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Per capita monthly household income (PCHI)

* subjected to means testing and meeting eligibility criteria
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment

sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.

*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)
sections.How to apply?:
- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**
  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass
2. **Hardcopy submission**
  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:
  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)
  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)
sections.What to expect?:
- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.
- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.

title: Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP)
description: ADAP supports caregivers of children without mental capacity to apply to be court-appointed deputies, through the simplified deputyship process. As a deputy, the caregiver can make legal decisions for the child when he/she turns 21.
highlights: Guidance provided for simplified deputyship applications for caregivers of persons with disabilities and without mental capacity
Acceptance of mental capacity assessment reports from SPED Schools, DACs, SWs, or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency

sections.About this support:
- Programme provides guidance/facilitation, for caregivers of persons with no mental capacity to manage their own matters in adulthood, to apply to Family Justice Courts to be appointed as legal deputies for their child. This is a simplified process that is also more affordable, compared to application for deputyship under standard route.
- Courts may accept mental capacity assessment reports prepared by psychologists from Special Education Schools (SPED Schools), selected Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency in lieu of a medical report. This applies only when the child is enrolled in a SPED school, DAC, or SW that is onboard the ADAP programme. In all other cases, the mental capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical doctor or psychiatrist.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Your child is:
  - between 18 and 21 years old as well as in the graduating cohort in a Special Education (SPED) school; or
  - above 18 years old and enrolled in an MSF-funded Day Activity Centre (DAC) or Sheltered Workshop (SW).
- You agree to use the standard list of powers/orders available under the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS) when filing a simplified Deputyship application.
- All family members and any other caregivers agree for you to make the application (i.e. it is an uncontested case).
sections.How to apply?:
Caregivers can approach the relevant staff in the SPED school, Day Activity Centre or Sheltered Workshop to indicate interest to apply for Deputyship. The school or centre will work with an MSF-appointed ADAP Agency to guide the parent/caregiver in their Deputyship application.

For Caregivers whose child with disability is not enrolled in a service, please contact ADAP Agency directly via phone or email for enquiries on deputyship application.

title: Caregiver Training and Support Programme
description: Provides training and support to caregivers of persons with mental health conditions so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.

sections.About this support:
CTSP consists of the Caregivers-to-Caregivers (C2C) Programme and Engagement-to-Empowerment (E2E) Programme. C2C aims to provide caregivers with the knowledge and skills regarding caregiving so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.

C2C provides various types of training courses that range from 8 to 12 sessions and in 3 different languages, to cover general or specific mental health conditions. Through the C2C training courses, caregiver leaders are also identified and trained to volunteer as caregiver leaders to support other caregivers in subsequent C2C classes and /or outreach and advocacy work.

E2E consists of the following components:

- Caregiver-for-Caregiver (C4C) Support Programme: 12 support group sessions over a year, with the aim of increasing support networks for caregivers. The first six sessions will be held in-person and will aim to provide support and equip caregivers with coping skills. Subsequent sessions may be a mix of online or in-person sessions, including self-run activities by caregivers with support from Mindfull Community Limited staff, to gather fellow caregivers for social activities or a sharing session.
- Train-the-Trainer (TTT): Caregivers who indicated interest to contribute and identified by staff as having potential are coached and trained as Volunteer Trainers and/or to support advocacy and outreach work through “Train-the-Trainer” modules so they can volunteer to support CAL’s programmes and activities.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Caregivers of Persons with Mental Health Issues (PMHIs).
- This can range from spouses, partners, parents, siblings, grandchildren, friends, neighbours, etc of someone who is experiencing a mental health condition.
sections.How to apply?: Register online through the [form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl).

title: Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)
description: A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.

sections.About this support: An LPA allows you to appoint trusted individuals to make decisions on (i) personal welfare and (ii) property and affairs, on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.
sections.Who is this for?:
Donors must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions
- Not be an undischarged bankrupt if you wish to make an LPA for property and affairs matters

Donees must:

- Be 21 years old and above
- Be your spouse or partner, family member or relative, friend, or a licensed trust company for property and affair matters only
- Have the mental capacity to make their own decisions
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

- [Apply online](https://opg-eservice.msf.gov.sg/) or
- You may also [book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance
  for your application. Please note that a [LPA certificate issuer](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa) is required to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make a LPA.
sections.What to expect?:
Here are the steps on how to make an LPA:

- Step 1: Decide on the type of LPA form
  - LPA Form 1 grants general powers to Donee(s) who will make decisions on your behalf when you lose mental capacity
  - LPA Form 2 is for applicants who want to appoint more than 2 Donees and/or more than 1 replacement Donee, and grant specific or customised powers that are not in the scope of LPA Form 1. You will need to engage a lawyer for LPA Form 2.
- Step 2: [Find an LPA certificate issuer ](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa)who is:
  - A medical professional accredited by the OPG
  - A registered psychiatrist
  - A practising lawyer (excluding lawyers registered under section 36E of the Legal Profession Act 1966)
- You and the LPA certificate issuer must digitally sign the LPA using the Singpass app. Your Donees can sign electronically by accepting their appointment.
- For your LPA to be legally valid, the certificate issuer must submit the LPA application to Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) via OPG Online (OPGO), as authorised by you.

title: Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)
description: Enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.
highlights: Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on
Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount
Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail

sections.About this support:
- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.
- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.
sections.Who is this for?:
The nominating applicant should be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs

The child with special needs should:

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

**Or**

- is attending or had attended a Special Education School

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.

Find out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification

You can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:

- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824
- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

You'll need to provide copies of:

- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC
- Child's Birth Certificate

If your child's disability status has not been verified:

- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or
- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*

After mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.

*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.

title: CPF Nomination
description: Allows you to decide what happens to your CPF savings after your death.

sections.About this support:
A CPF nomination allows you to decide:

- Who will receive your CPF savings (your “nominee”)
- The percentage of your CPF savings each nominee should receive
- CPF savings **cannot be distributed by a will **as CPF savings do not form part of your estate. This arrangement **protects your CPF savings from creditor claims** on any outstanding debts you may have and preserves your savings fully for your nominees.

Your CPF nomination will cover:

- CPF savings in your Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts
- CPF LIFE premium balance
- Your discounted Singtel shares (if any)

Your CPF nomination does not cover:

- Properties bought using your CPF savings
- Payout from the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)
- Investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)
sections.Who is this for?:
To make a CPF nomination, you must:

- Be a CPF member
- Be aged 16 years and above
- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions

You can **nominate any person or legal entity*** to be the beneficiary of your CPF savings.

*An entity that is capable of receiving monies in its own right.
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

- Apply [online](http://cpf.gov.sg/MakeCPFNOM) using your Singpass
- [Make an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form) to apply in person at any CPF service centre if you are unable to find two witnesses
- [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) to visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) for in-person guidance on your online nomination application. Click [here](https://www.psd.gov.sg/servicesg/) for the list of ServiceSG Centres and their operating hours

**For online application**

You will need to have:

**Your nominees’ particulars**

1. Full Name
2. NRIC or Foreign Identification Number (FIN)
3. Mailing Address (for foreigners)
4. Email Address (optional)

**Two witnesses’ particulars**

1. Full Name
2. NRIC
3. Email address and/or Singapore-registered mobile phone number
4. Cannot be a nominee
5. He/she cannot be a nominee and must be at least 21 years of age

Upon submission of your nomination,** inform your witnesses to log in **[here](http://cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM)** within 7 calendar days to witness your nomination using their Singpass.**

**For in-person application**

You will need to bring along and prepare:

- A copy of your NRIC/passport
- Your nominee(s)' NRIC number or Foreign Identification Number (FIN), email (optional), and mailing address (for foreigners)

As CPF Board's customer service executives or ServiceSG staff are acting as your witnesses, you do not need to prepare your witnesses' particulars.
sections.What to expect?:
If your nominee falls into the following categories, here is what to expect:

**Below 18 Years Old**
The monies will be held in trust by the Public Trustee until your nominee turns 18.
**Unable To Make Decisions Independently**
The monies will be handled by their court appointed deputy.
**Bankrupt**
The monies belonging to the undischarged bankrupt nominee, will be transferred to the Official Assignee.

To allow your CPF savings to be distributed swiftly according to your wishes when you pass on, it is important to **review your CPF nomination regularly**, especially at key milestones (e.g.):

- Starting Work
- Marriage*
- Childbirth
- Divorce
- Death of a nominee
- When you reach your golden years**

*Your nomination will be revoked upon marriage, and you should make a new nomination.

**Review your nomination and consider your current family circumstances, such as which family member may need your savings more.

title: Advance Care Planning (ACP)
description: Helps communicate your values and how they shape your healthcare preferences to your loved ones and healthcare team.

sections.About this support:
Advance Care Planning (ACP) is an ongoing process of planning and preparing for your future health and personal care. It includes conversations about your:

- personal beliefs
- values
- healthcare preferences

These will be shared with your loved ones and healthcare team.

Having a quality ACP ensures that this process is person-centred, informed and guided. In the event that you lose the capacity to make decisions or speak for yourself, the ACP will help your loved ones and healthcare team act in your best interests based on your prior expressed wishes.
sections.Who is this for?:
- For any individuals aged 21 years old* and above who has the capacity to make their own decisions.
- Includes people who are healthy and living with chronic or any other medical conditions.

ACP is particularly important for people who are living with a health condition. You can consult your regular doctor, especially if you have chronic conditions (e.g. diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease) or any other medical concerns.

*For individuals below 21 years old and living with a health condition, please approach your healthcare team if you are interested to find out more about ACP.
sections.How to apply?:
You can:

1. Use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/)

Complete your ACP without having to speak to an ACP facilitator. You can use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/) if you:

- have a Singpass account
- are at least 21 years old
- do not have any existing serious illness
- do not have a Preferred Plan of Care (PPC) ACP or Disease Specific (DS) ACP

Once you’ve completed the online form, your NHS will receive digital invitations. They’ll be notified via SMS, and must accept or reject their appointment by logging in to My Legacy with their Singpass. Your ACP will automatically be registered once all your NHS have accepted their appointments.

1. Book an appointment with an ACP facilitator

[Visit an ACP service provider](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/listing/acp-providers/results) if you:

- prefer to have a conversation with an ACP facilitator and be guided
- have an existing serious illness*

Your ACP will be registered in the National Electronic Health Records (NEHR) upon completing all discussions with your facilitator. Some service providers may charge a nominal fee. Please check with the respective organisation for details.

* Serious illnesses include: Cancer, Stroke, End Stage Renal Failure (ESRF), Severe Liver Disease, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), Dementia, and Chronic Neurological Disease.

1. [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance for your application.

You may also refer to [this website](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/end-of-life-planning/advance-care-planning/) for more information on steps to prepare your ACP.
sections.What to expect?:
- You will need to appoint a Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS) who is responsible for speaking on your behalf about your healthcare preferences when you are no longer able to do so. In such situations, the healthcare team will consult your NHS and discuss your care plan.
- After completing your ACP, it will be available on the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR), where your healthcare team can access and refer to your ACP to prepare your care plan.

title: Settling Outstanding Tax Matters and Bills for a Deceased Person
description: Enables executors or administrators to settle the deceased's taxes and outstanding debts using the estate's funds before distribution to beneficiaries.
highlights: Settle the deceased's taxes and debts using the estate's funds

sections.About this support:
Executors or administrators of a deceased can act on the deceased’s following matters:

- Filing personal income tax for the deceased on the income earned up to the date of death.
- Filing estate or trust income tax for the deceased on the income. Estate income refers to the income generated by the deceased’s assets after date of death, during the administration of the estate. Trust income refers to the income from assets held in trust.
- Settling the taxes and other bills such as loans, funeral expenses and medical bills from the estate funds of the deceased before distribution to deceased’s beneficiaries.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Executors or administrators of a deceased’s estate who are responsible for settling outstanding taxes, debts and liabilities.
- Remember, the executor or administrator must ensure all outstanding taxes, loans, funeral expenses, and medical bills are paid from the deceased's estate before distributing the remaining assets to the beneficiaries.
sections.How to apply?:
File personal income tax for the deceased
Provide IRAS with the following details via [myTaxMail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/portal/correspondence/mytax-mail):
- Name, address and identification number of the legal personal representative who is handling the affairs of the deceased;
- Copy of the death certificate;
- Copy of the Grant of Probate/Letter of Administration, if available;
- Income details from all sources, up to the date of death (please specify the breakdown for each income source); and
- Type and amount of tax relief available/applicable to reduce the tax burden.
File an Income Tax Return for Estate or Trust Income
- Download and complete the Request Form for Form T from [IRAS's website](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/other-taxes/trusts/filing-estate-trust-income-tax-(form-t)/form-t).
- Email the completed form to [trust@iras.gov.sg ](mailto:trust@iras.gov.sg)and IRAS will provide you with:
  - a Trust Reference Number
  - a copy of Form T to complete
- Mail the completed Form T to this address: The Comptroller of Income Tax, 55 Newton Road, Singapore 307987.

title: MediFund
description: For Singaporeans who face difficulties with remaining medical bills after receiving government subsidies and other means of payment.
highlights: Assistance with medical bills
Amount of assistance depends on the applicant's circumstances and bills incurred
Apply through Medical Social Workers at the institution where you received treatment

sections.About this support: The actual amount of assistance you receive depends on you and your family members' financial, health and social circumstances, as well as the size of the medical bill incurred.
sections.How to apply?:
- You or your family can approach the Medical Social Workers at the MediFund-approved institution at which you had treatment
- In addition to MediFund, they will also be able to explore other possible financing means with you
sections.Phone number:
MediFund applications are administered directly by the MediFund-approved institution. You may wish to first contact the Medical Social Services Department or Business Office Department of the institution you are seeking care at for further assistance.

MOH Hotline: [6325 9220](tel:63259220)

title: Pioneer Generation Package
description: Special recognition to our Pioneer Generation through a package that assures them of affordable healthcare.
highlights: Provides our Pioneer Generation with a special package that ensures affordable healthcare
Benefits include life-long monthly cash assistance and healthcare subsidies

sections.About this support:
Provides the following benefits to support healthcare for Pioneers:

MediSave Top-Ups
- Annual MediSave top-ups for life, ranging from $300 to $1,200 depending on birth cohort, to offset premiums for MediShield Life, ElderShield and CareShield Life.
- Additional MediSave top-ups of $50 to $200 will be disbursed from 2021 to 2025 for older Pioneers (i.e. those aged 82 and above in 2021) with serious pre-existing conditions who are paying additional premiums.
Additional Outpatient Care Subsidies
- Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.
Special MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
- Supports Pioneers in paying their MediShield Life premiums with special premium subsidies of up to 60%.
- Combined with the MediSave top-ups ($300 - $1,200), Pioneers born in 1934 or earlier will see their MediShield Life premiums fully covered, and Pioneers born from 1935 to 1949 will have about two-thirds of their MediShield Life premiums covered.
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme
- Grants life-long cash assistance of $100 each month for those needing permanent assistance with at least 3 out of 6 of the following Activities of Daily Living:
  - Eating
  - Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Transferring
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
[Incentives have ceased]
CareShield Life Additional Participation Incentives
- Provides participation incentives (totalling $3,000) to encourage Pioneers to join CareShield Life by 31 Dec 2024, in addition to any other premium subsidies seniors may receive.

If you would like [more details on the above benefits as well as other useful information about this Package, please refer here.](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/pioneer-generation-package)
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- Born on or before 31 December 1949 and acquired citizenship on or before 31 December 1986
- Eligible applicants have been notified in 2014
- You may check your eligibility by:
  - Using the LifeSG app to view your Pioneer Generation e-card; or
  - Logging in to the Singpass mobile app to view your eligibility status
sections.How to apply?:
- No application required
- Eligible individuals will receive the benefits automatically
- To apply for the Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS), visit [this site](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/pioneer-generation-disability-assistance-scheme/) for more information

For loss of Pioneer Generation Card, and other healthcare-related enquiries: [1800-650-6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

title: Deputyship
description: For persons who lack mental capacity and have not made a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and/or have no donee to make certain decisions on their behalf.

sections.About this support:
- Deputyship is required if a person has lost mental capacity and did not appoint a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)
- A deputy may be the patient's family member or friend
sections.Who is this for?: Persons who have been certified to have no mental capacity.
sections.How to apply?: [Find out more on how to apply for a deputyship](https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/family/deputyship)
sections.What to expect?:
- You may apply to the court to seek a court order to be appointed as a Deputy.
- Anyone above 21 years of age can apply to be a Deputy. A Deputy is usually a family member or close friend who would act in the best interest of the person who lacks capacity.
- A doctor has to certify that the patient lacks mental capacity to make decisions due to an impairment of or disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain
- The Family Courts hear all deputyship applications under the Mental Capacity Act
- Applicants may need to fulfil the services’ in-take criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any.

title: Professional Deputies and Donees Scheme
description: The scheme serves individuals who may not have suitable family members or friends to appoint as their proxy decision makers. Professionals may be appointed as proxy decision makers for these individuals for remuneration.
highlights: Professional deputies have to pass a certification course and a list of stringent criteria (e.g.  no history of bankruptcy or criminal proceedings related to financial dishonesty) before they can be registered
The professional deputies have to re-register every 2 years with the Office of the Public Guardian to ensure they still meet the stringent criteria
The charges of the Professional Deputies vary depending on their professions and individual case requirements. Individuals may engage them to mutually agree on the fee charge

sections.About this support:
- Professionals registered under this scheme include lawyers, doctors, accountants, allied health professionals, nurses, and social workers
- Professional deputies apply to Court to act for individuals who lack mental capacity (known as 'P') on property &, affairs, and personal welfare matters
- Professional deputies provide a (i) P-focused plan and a (ii) Schedule of Assets as part of the application
sections.Who is this for?:
- Persons who lack mental capacity (known as ‘P’) who do not have suitable family members or friends to be their proxy decision makers
- Individuals with mental capacity can also choose to make a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), and appoint a Professional Deputy to act as a Donee for renumeration
sections.How to apply?: Members of the public who are keen to appoint a professional deputy/donee can approach any of the individuals on this [list of Registered Professional Deputies/Donees](https://www.msf.gov.sg/docs/default-source/opg/list_of_registered_professional_deputies.pdf?sfvrsn=83247f26_98) to enquire on their professional fees and to make an appointment.
sections.Where to go: [Family@Enabling Village 20 Lengkok Bahru, #04-02 Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)
sections.Email / Form: [Submit an enquiry](https://ask.gov.sg/msf/questions/new?topic=MSF Office of the Public Guardian)

MSF Consolidated Hotline: [1800-111-2222](tel:18001112222) 
(To reach the Office of the Public Guardian, say "OPG" when prompted by the virtual assistant)

title: My Legacy
description: Plan, store and share your legal, healthcare and estate matters securely with people you trust.

sections.About this support:
- My Legacy is a trusted digital companion that makes planning easy and convenient.
- It uses technology to make it seamless to document and share your plans, so that you and your loved ones can spend the time focusing on the things that matter: celebrating your relationships, achieving your life goals, and leaving a lasting legacy.
sections.Who is this for?: - Individuals aged 30 and above who are interested to find out how they can start their legacy planning.
sections.How to apply?:
- No application is needed
- [Find out more on how to start legacy planning](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/end-of-life-planning)
sections.What to expect?:
- Consolidated information on legacy planning and services like applying for a Lasting Power of Attorney, Advance Care Planning
- [You can also download a copy of a deceased's digital death certificate from My Legacy if it is still within 30 days from the date of issuance.](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/download-death-or-stillbirth-certificate/)

title: MediShield Life
description: A basic health insurance plan managed by the CPF Board to help pay for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatments.
highlights: Lifetime coverage for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents regardless of age or health condition
No application needed

sections.About this support:
- Provides [lifetime coverage](https://moh.gov.sg/home/our-healthcare-system/medishield-life/what-is-medishield-life/what-medishield-life-benefits) for hospital bills and selected outpatient treatments
- MediShield Life coverage is sized for subsidised treatment in public hospitals and pegged at B2/C-type wards
- If you choose to stay in an A/B1-type ward or in a private hospital, you are still covered by MediShield Life
  - However, your MediShield Life payout will cover only a proportion of your bill, and you would need to draw from MediSave and/or cash to pay the balance
sections.Who is this for?: - Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
sections.How to apply?: No application is required

title: MediSave
description: A personal healthcare savings account that helps you pay for you and loved ones' healthcare expenses over your lifetime, especially when you retire and no longer have regular income.
highlights: Covers selected medical, treatment and hospital expenses, up to the approved limits
Covers for healthcare insurance premiums, rehabilitation and palliative care
Applicable at all MediSave accredited Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs)

sections.About this support:
- MediSave pays for a variety of medical expenses such as selected outpatient treatments, day surgery and hospitalisation expenses
- It also covers the costs for your rehabilitation and palliative care
- You can also tap on your MediSave to pay for health insurance premiums for yourself and your loved ones
sections.Who is this for?:
- You need to be a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR)
- Your spouse, children and parents can be of any nationality, except grandparents and siblings who must be SC or PR
sections.How to apply?:
- To use your MediSave, inform the Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs) or Medical Institutions (MIs) where you are receiving treatment at, and you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your medical expenses
  - If this is your first time applying, you will need to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)
  - If you had previously given a standing authorisation for the use of MediSave, the MI will submit a claim on your behalf
- The PHI and/or MI will submit the medical claim on your behalf and payment from your healthcare plans will be made directly to them
- Upon approval of the claim, the Board and/or insurer will notify you accordingly
sections.Where to go:
[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)
Note: By appointment only
sections.Phone number:
Healthcare Hotline: [1800 222 3399](tel:18002223399)

To avoid waiting on the line, you may book an appointment [here](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form).

title: Live Well, Age Well Programme
description: The Live Well, Age Well programme is co-organised by HPB and PA to provide holistic activities to improve the physical, mental and social health of adults aged 50 and above.
highlights: Discover free activities near you to stay healthy and active
Download the Healthy 365 mobile app on Apple Store / Google Play

sections.About this support:
- As we age, staying healthy and active is important so you can continue doing the activities you love.
- The Live Well, Age Well programme features a wide range of FREE^ exciting activities in your neighbourhood to help you kickstart your healthy living journey.
- Activities are specially designed based on the needs of adults aged 50 years old and above, so as to help you improve your physical, mental and social health to continue doing what you love.
- These programmes are available at multiple locations near you, including Community Centres/Clubs, Residents’ Committee, Residents’ Network Centres, Senior Activity Centres. Some programmes (e.g. group exercise sessions and workshops) are also available online, so you can stay healthy in the comfort of your home.

^Except for subsidised health screening programmes under Live Assured.
sections.Who is this for?:
- All Singapore residents aged 50 and above are welcome to join our Live Well, Age Well programme.
- There may be additional criteria for selected programmes.
- Visit [Live Well, Age Well website](https://www.healthhub.sg/programmes/160/AAP) for more information.
sections.How to apply?:
**Step 1**: Download the Healthy 365 mobile app on Apple Store / Google Play.

**Step 2**: Create profile if you are a new user. Log in to your existing profile with your NRIC and registered phone number if you are an existing user.

**Step 3**: Tap on "Explore" and select "Events" to view upcoming events.

**Step 4**: Search "Active Ageing" to filter for Live Well, Age Well programmes.

**Step 5**: Select the event you are interested in to view more details. Select "Book Now" to sign up.

You may also visit your nearest Community Clubs/Centres (CCs) or Residents’ Committees (RC)/Residents’ Network (RN) Centres for assistance.

highlights: Provides various health-related benefits to support seniors’ ageing, such as additional Outpatient Care subsidies and additional MediShield (MSHL) premium subsidies

title: Car Park Label Scheme
description: Provides two types of labels that allow drivers (Class 1) and passengers (Class 2) with medically certified mobility challenges to park at accessible spaces, so they can board or alight from their vehicles safely.
highlights: Eligible drivers and passengers with mobility impairment can apply for a Car Park Label to use accessible lots

sections.About this support:
- Car park labels allow access to accessible lots for easier boarding and alighting for drivers and passengers with mobility impairment
- Each label can be used by the label holder only. Car park labels are not applicable to motorcycles
- Option for Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to obtain labels for vehicles providing dedicated transport to passengers with mobility impairment
sections.Who is this for?:
- For Class 1: Drivers who are certified by Singapore registered medical professionals to require the use of bulky mobility aids and need to open the vehicle doors fully to board or alight from the vehicle.
- For Class 2: Passengers who are certified by a Singapore registered medical professionals as to require the use of bulky mobility aids and need to open the vehicle doors fully to board or alight from the vehicle.
- For Class 2 SSA: Social Service Agencies registered as NCSS Members providing dedicated transport to passengers with mobility impairment.
sections.How to apply?: For more information on the application process, please visit [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/car-park-label-scheme).

title: MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
description: To keep MediShield Life premiums affordable, the Government provides several premium support measures, such as Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
highlights: Premium subsidies of up to 60%
Pioneer and Merdeka Generation subsidies

sections.About this support:
**Eligibility criteria for Premium Subsidies:**

- Premium Subsidies of up to 60% for eligible lower-to middle-income households
- Pioneer Generation Subsidies of between 40-60%, depending on age
- Merdeka Generation Subsidies of between 5%-10%, depending on age

As of 1 Apr 2025,

Household Monthly Income Per Person
Subsidy Range (tiered by age)
$0 - $1,500
25% - 60%
> $1,501 - $2,600
20% - 55%
> $2,601 - $3,600
15% - 40%

Note: The above subsidy rates apply to those living in property with an AV of $21,000 or less. Properties with an AV between $21,001 and $31,000 receive 10% less subsidies. Permanent Residents (PRs) receive half the subsidy rate applicable to Singapore Citizens (SCs). Those who live in residences with an AV above $31,000 or own multiple properties will not receive these subsidies.

**Eligibility for Pioneer Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Pioneers, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence

**Eligibility for Merdeka Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Merdeka Generation seniors, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence, on top of the Premium Subsidies that the seniors may be eligible for

Please [click here](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
sections.Who is this for?:
Eligibility criteria for Premium Subsidies:

- Household monthly income per person of $3,600 or below; and
- Living in property with an Annual Value (AV) of $31,000 and below; and
- Not owning more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?: The subsidies that you are eligible for will be automatically applied to your MediShield Life premiums.
